title: Group maps on initial intervals
summary: Let $S$ denote a $k$-subset of $\mathbb{Z}$. Let $G$ be a (multiplicative) group of size $k$. Assume that there exists a function $\varphi\colon S \to G$ that is injective and that satisfies the following: If $x, y, z \in S$ and $z = xy$, then $\varphi(z) = \varphi(x) \varphi(y)$. In 1990, Forcade and Pollington conjectured that if $S = \{ 1, 2, \ldots, k \}$, then $G$ is abelian. This has been a long-standing conjecture highlighted by Richard K. Guy as an unsolved problem, and this problem appears to have remained open, with its open status having been noted by Caicedo et al. in 2021…
